title: Sequence-guided SSE resumption and semantic chunk anchors
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a robust SSE-based streaming resume mechanism that uses sequence-guided anchors embedded in chunk metadata to allow safe, idempotent resumption across client disconnects. This ticket covers protocol extension (headers and chunk envelope), server-side windowing and retention semantics, client compatibility shim for legacy clients, and alignment guarantees for function/tool-call boundaries and structured JSON outputs.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a per-stream monotonic sequence token and periodic 'anchor' events containing semantic boundary markers (function-call start/end, structured JSON integrity checkpoints).

Clients can reconnect with an explicit resume token header (X-Seq-Resume) and the server will re-send only overlapping chunks necessary to restore exactly to the last semantic anchor, guaranteeing tool-call atomicity or fail-safe truncate semantics.

Resume protocol works with both chunked JSONL structured outputs and function-call frames without producing duplicate side-effects (idempotency preserved for tool-call ops via server-side call dedup keys).

Legacy clients (no resume support) receive a graceful compatibility response that indicates non-resumable stream and includes an opt-in backwards-compatible framing marker so they can still parse outputs without corruption.
Perf regression <5% p90 latency for typical 128-token responses vs baseline, and memory retention bounded per stream with configurable retention window (default 30s/1MB whichever first).
E2E tests and stress harness included that simulate network flaps, reordered reconnections, and concurrent reconnections from multiple client IPs.
implementation_notes: Protocol: add header X-Seq-Token on initial handshake; server will include 'anchor' SSE events with type=anchor and payload: {seq, boundary_type, boundary_id, checksum}.
Chunk envelope: each data chunk will be JSONL with fields: seq, offset, payload, checksum; payload may include function_call frames encoded separately and tagged with boundary_id.
Retention: keep last N anchors and associated chunks per stream; default retention window is 30s or 1MB. Configurable per-customer on Dedicated plans.
Resume logic: on reconnect with X-Seq-Resume, server validates seq and serves minimal replay window; if seq expired, fallback to full stream restart and emit 'resume_lost' event.

Idempotency for tool-calls: server assigns call-dedup-id for each function invocation; replays will not re-execute calls if dedup-id already seen—call status persisted to short-lived call cache with TTL aligned to retention window.
Compatibility shim: if client lacks resume headers, server emits a 'compat-v1' framing header and anchors will be no-op markers so older clients can ignore but preserve stream integrity.
Observability: emit telemetry events for resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_expired, anchor_emitted with stream_id and token; add dashboard panel in Console runtime-1.24.
API changes: SDKs (JS/Python/Go) will get helper util to persist resume token and transparently attempt resume; default enabled for hosted API, opt-out via client config.
comments: 2025-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial scoping complete. Chosen sequence-anchor design to avoid heavyweight per-token state. Added retention knobs for Dedicated customers.

2025-02-24 - Luca Moretti: Prototype server-side anchor emitter implemented on streaming branch. Observed ~3.2% p95 overhead in local bench for 128-token streams. Need to optimize JSONL envelope allocation.

2025-02-26 - Cristina Gomez (review): Reviewed design doc; request to clarify checksum algorithm (prefer blake2b-64) and to include an explicit 'anchor-signature' header for cross-region verification.
2025-02-27 - Luca Moretti: Updated implementation notes to use blake2b-64 and added 'anchor-sign' optional header. Raised PR for server changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8372

2025-03-01 - QA: Created stress tests in infra-harness simulating 2000 simultaneous reconnects; observed a small window where duplicate function-call dedup keys were expired too early—investigating TTL alignment.

2025-03-02 - PM (Harper Lee): Confirming customer_impact high due to several enterprise customers requesting resumable streams for large structured outputs. Prioritize stability over aggressive retention to avoid silent truncation.
qa_plan: Unit tests for anchor emission and parsing, including malformed anchor payloads.
Integration tests: simulate reconnect sequences with exact seq, expired seq, and mismatched region seq.
E2E with SDKs: JS and Python clients automatically persisting resume token and validating no duplicate tool-call side effects.
Load test: verify memory boundedness with long-lived 50k active streams and retention window enforced.
